scholarships.title: International Visegrad Fund Fellowships and Scholarships (V4 mobility)

existing.description: The International Visegrad Fund runs regional mobility programmes for Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Ukraine. The Visegrad Fellowship Program funds individual short-term in-person stays of 2 to 10 weeks for full-time doctoral students and PhD holders to conduct a research project, give lectures or seminars, or study archival material at an institution in a V4 country other than their country of citizenship and residence; it pays a lump-sum scholarship of EUR 500 per week in two instalments (80% and 20%). The separate Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers for up to two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe and its next cycle opens on 1 January 2027. Other Fund programmes include the Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships for doctoral and post-doctoral researchers, the Western Balkans-Visegrad Fellowships, research grants at the Historical Archives of the EU, and a scholarship at the Open Society Archives in Budapest.

National of Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia or Ukraine
Country of citizenship and residence must differ from the host institution's country within the V4 region
Master's or post-Master's status for the Visegrad Scholarship Program
Doctoral or post-doctoral status for the Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships

Visegrad Scholarship: supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers. Visegrad-Taiwan: doctoral and post-doctoral researchers from V4 countries.

existing.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated on academic credentials or work experience including the publication record and recommendation letter; the coherence and justification of the research plan including lectures, presentations and final publications; and the regional relevance of the topic with justification of the host. Reapplying is possible, but preference is always given to fellows not yet supported and to previous fellows whose proposals build on past findings or change the host institution or country.
existing.best_fit: Students from V4, Western Balkans, and Eastern Partnership countries studying in Czech Republic
existing.notes: The Fund asks candidates to avoid reapplying within the same term (January through May, or September through November) regardless of the outcome, and notes that repeated support is possible only in exceptional cases where continuation is justified.
existing.duration: Max 2 semesters at master’s or post-Master’s (doctoral, postdoc) degree levels.
existing.application_period: Visegrad Fellowship Program: the current call opened 1 September 2026 and closes 30 November 2026 at 12:00. The Fund also states that applications are accepted through the My Visegrad system continuously in two periods, January through May and September through November, but only while capacities last. The Visegrad Scholarship Program opens 1 January 2027.

existing.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program supports full-time Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for one to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. It is funded by the International Visegrad Fund, founded by the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia. The award is EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution, and it does not cover tuition. Applicants must already hold a bachelor's or master's degree, and their country of citizenship or residence must differ from the host institution's country.

Be a citizen or resident of a Czech, Hungarian, Polish or Slovak nationality (V4), or of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, Northern Macedonia, Serbia or Ukraine (EaP/WB)
The country of the applicant's citizenship must be different from the country of the host institution
Previous levels of university studies must have been completed in a country other than the one where the scholarship is applied for
The distance between the applicant's current employer/university or permanent residence and the host university or institute should exceed 150 km
Study or research period of 1-2 semesters, full-time, at master's or post-master's level
